target.title: fix(deepinfra): apply request policy to video generation requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where DeepInfra video generation requests ignored configured provider request controls, so custom headers, proxy routing, and private-network permission could fail to reach the real transport.

## Why This Change Was Made

The DeepInfra video generation path now sanitizes the configured provider request policy and passes it into the shared HTTP resolver. The call-site `allowPrivateNetwork: false` override was removed because it took precedence over an explicit configured `true`; the resolver still defaults omitted configuration to fail closed.

This is an AI-assisted contribution prepared for Alix-007.

## User Impact

Operators using DeepInfra video generation can apply the same request headers, proxy routing, and private-network controls as other provider transports. Existing configurations that omit or explicitly disable private-network access remain blocked by default.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `f5128c8fed61fc52feca0119d848b6d6aba706c5` (rebuilt as three substantive commits on `upstream/main` `210340fe937b6dc1c95ed82970384d6de6a06c58`).
- Focused proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/deepinfra/video-generation-provider.transport.test.ts extensions/deepinfra/video-generation-provider.test.ts --run --reporter verbose`
- Result: 2 test files passed, 14 tests passed.
- Real transport proof: configured `allowPrivateNetwork: true` reached a loopback DeepInfra endpoint, sent `POST /v1/inference/Pixverse/Pixverse-T2V`, exposed the custom `X-DeepInfra-Trace: transport-proof` header to the server, and decoded the returned video.
- Proxy proof: configured `request.proxy.mode: env-proxy` produced an observed HTTP `CONNECT` tunnel to the target host, and the upstream DeepInfra fixture received the request through that tunnel.
- Fail-closed proof: omitted request configuration and explicit `allowPrivateNetwork: false` both failed before the loopback server received any request.
- `oxfmt --check` on all three changed files: passed.
- Direct locked-version `oxlint` on all three changed files: passed.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`: passed.
- Repository `run-oxlint` wrapper did not reach target lint because its extension-boundary declaration preflight hit existing shared dependency hydration mismatches in `packages/net-policy/src/ip.ts` and `src/infra/push-web.ts`; these files are outside this diff. The target-file lint above passed.
- Validation used the repo-native narrow local fallback because Crabbox/Testbox was unavailable. It temporarily reused the shared checkout's installed dependencies; no dependency install, lockfile change, or committed link was made.
- Autoreview: Codex isolation could not authenticate (HTTP 401, no review result); the documented Claude fallback (`claude-sonnet-4-6`, high) completed clean with no accepted/actionable findings.

### Exact-head proof continuity (immutable no-runtime-diff)
- Current PR head: `e492a3db16edfd2c5b102c060451fd97065dbfc4`.
- Previously proven candidate: `f5128c8fed61fc52feca0119d848b6d6aba706c5` (the loopback, proxy, header, and fail-closed transport proof described above).
- The GitHub Contents API returned identical Git blob SHAs for every changed file:
  - `extensions/deepinfra/video-generation-provider.test.ts`: old `c28289a7339de61a8c180105f7c50336dc739840` = current `c28289a7339de61a8c180105f7c50336dc739840`
  - `extensions/deepinfra/video-generation-provider.transport.test.ts`: old `5c11c18667f0ea5251aac65212a3307cbad65fda` = current `5c11c18667f0ea5251aac65212a3307cbad65fda`
  - `extensions/deepinfra/video-generation-provider.ts`: old `4fadd5660697f3bda47212ef120497521d7afa23` = current `4fadd5660697f3bda47212ef120497521d7afa23`
- Exact-head CI context: [run 29716251997](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29716251997), required CI lanes passed; the repository proof-context check passed in [run 29716251470](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29716251470).
- Reproduction boundary: this is an immutable source-equivalence proof, not a claim of a new network execution. All 3 changed source/test blobs are identical to the previously proven candidate, so the prior configured-private-network, proxy, and fail-closed behavior applies to the current head.
- `PROOF_RESULT=PASS` (3/3 changed files identical; no runtime/test diff after the prior transport proof).
